name: Shalmali Joshi
bio: Dr. Joshi is an Assistant Professor at Columbia University, Department of Biomedical Informatics where she leads the reAIM Lab. She works to advance Machine Learning (ML) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) methods with the goal of advancing clinical health and medicine for all.

name: Divyam Madaan
bio: Divyam Madaan is a Postdoctoral Fellow in Biomedical Informatics, Columbia University. Prior to Columbia, he earned his Ph.D. from New York University, advised by Sumit Chopra and Kyunghyun Cho. His research focuses on developing models that can effectively learn from multiple modalities and generalize across distribution shifts, with a special emphasis on healthcare applications. His work has been published at leading venues including ICML, NeurIPS, CVPR and ICLR, where he has also been recognized with oral and spotlight presentation awards.

name: Young Sang Choi
bio: Young is a doctoral student in Biomedical Informatics advised by Dr. Shalmali Joshi and Dr. Pierre Elias. His research sits at the intersection of multimodal learning, event stream modeling, and trustworthy machine learning. He is particularly interested in how these fields converge to create reliable AI-based systems that advance human health.  Previously, he was a researcher at the National Cancer Center-Korea, received a master's degree under the supervision of Dr. Deborah Estrin in Information Systems at Cornell Tech, and graduated from New York University with a bachelor's degree in Mathematics.

name: Aparajita Kashyap
bio: Aparajita (Apara) Kashyap is a PhD student at Columbia University in the Department of Biomedical Informatics. Her research focuses on building fair and equitable models for use in healthcare settings, with a focus on mental health disorders and reproductive health disorders. At Columbia, Aparajita is coadvised by Shalmali Joshi and Noémie Elhadad. Prior to her work at Columbia, Aparajita studied Biophysics at Johns Hopkins University.

name: Yuta Kobayashi
bio: Yuta is a doctoral student in Biomedical Informatics advised by Dr. Shalmali Joshi. He received his bachelor's degree in Computer Science and Biomedical Engineering and a master's degree in Computer Science at Johns Hopkins University, where he was advised by Dr. Archana Venkataraman. Currently, his research focuses on utilizing tools from causal inference and reinforcement learning to detect and mitigate algorithmic bias in AI models for healthcare.

name: Zilin Jing
bio: Zilin is a doctoral student in Computer Science advised by Dr. Shalmali Joshi. He received his bachelor's degree in Computer Science and Engineering at The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen under the supervision of Prof. Shuang Li and Prof. Hongyuan Zha and was an international visiting student at Yale University through Y-VISP. His research interests are in machine learning for healthcare, causal inference and reinforcement learning.

name: Ananya Chavadhal
bio: Ananya is a doctoral student in Computer Science advised by Dr. Shalmali Joshi. She received her bachelor’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, with a minor in Computer Science, from the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, where she was advised by Dr. Saket Choudhary. Her research interests lie in machine learning methods for biomedical problems. When not working, she enjoys running, painting, reading and solving crosswords.
